name: Nurul Amin
contribution: Nurul Amin became East Bengal's chief minister in 1948 and led the provincial government during the early years of Pakistan's rule.
context: His administration operated amid disputes over provincial autonomy, representation, and the status of Bengali, while the Muslim League faced growing opposition in East Bengal.
impact: His opposition to the Bengali-language demand became part of the political context in which the Language Movement weakened the Muslim League's authority before the 1954 United Front victory.
seoDescription: Profile of Nurul Amin, tracing connections to the 1947 Partition, Eastern Bengal, and related political-cultural history.
shortAnswer: Nurul Amin is linked to the 1947 Partition in this timeline as East Bengal Chief Minister.

faq.question: How is Nurul Amin connected to the 1947 Partition?
faq.answer: Nurul Amin served as East Bengal's chief minister from 1948 to 1954. His government faced the language question and wider disputes over representation; his opposition to the Bengali-language demand is recorded in accounts of the Language Movement.
